cards.front: Recall a key point about The Behaviourist & Social Learning Approach
cards.back: Classical conditioning (Pavlov): learning by association. A neutral stimulus becomes associated with an unconditioned stimulus, producing a conditioned response. Pavlov's dogs: bell (NS) paired with food (UCS) -> salivation (UCR). After conditioning: bell alone (CS) -> salivation (CR). Explains phobias and emotional responses.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Behaviourist & Social Learning Approach
cards.back: Operant conditioning (Skinner): learning by consequences. Positive reinforcement: adding something pleasant to increase behaviour (reward). Negative reinforcement: removing something unpleasant to increase behaviour (taking painkillers removes pain). Punishment: adding something unpleasant to decrease behaviour. Skinner's Box: rats pressed a lever for food (positive reinforcement).

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Behaviourist & Social Learning Approach
cards.back: Social Learning Theory (Bandura): we learn by observing others. Key processes: attention (notice the behaviour), retention (remember it), reproduction (ability to copy it), motivation (want to copy it - influenced by vicarious reinforcement). Bandura's Bobo doll study: children who saw an aggressive model were significantly more aggressive.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Behaviourist & Social Learning Approach
cards.back: Mediational processes in SLT distinguish it from pure behaviourism: SLT acknowledges cognitive processes (attention, retention, motivation) mediate between stimulus and response. This makes SLT more comprehensive than traditional behaviourism.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Behaviourist & Social Learning Approach
cards.back: Applications: classical conditioning explains phobias and underpins systematic desensitisation. Operant conditioning explains token economies in institutions. SLT explains how aggression and gender roles are learned from media and role models.

cards.front: What should you know about psychology exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating behaviourism, always consider: is it too reductionist? Does it ignore cognition? Is it environmentally deterministic? Compare with the cognitive approach and SLT to show the development from strict behaviourism to cognitive-social approaches.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Behaviourism fully explains human behaviour because everything we do is learned through conditioning.
